Package com.macstab.chaos.jvm.api

@NullMarked package com.macstab.chaos.jvm.api
The public chaos API: plans, scenarios, selectors, effects, policies and the control plane.

Every type is non-null unless annotated @Nullable.

  • Class
    Description
    ActivationPolicy
    Controls when and how often a chaos effect fires when its selector matches an operation.
    ActivationPolicy.Builder
    Builder for ActivationPolicy.
    ActivationPolicy.RateLimit
    Fixed-window rate limit on effect applications.
    ActivationPolicy.StartMode
    Controls whether a scenario activates automatically on registration or waits for an explicit ChaosActivationHandle.start() call.
    AsyncChaosEventListener
    A listener the control plane calls on an agent-owned thread, through a bounded queue; created by ChaosEventListener.async(ChaosEventListener).
    ChaosActivationConflictException
    Thrown when a scenario cannot be activated because a live scenario with the same id is already active in the same scope.
    ChaosActivationException
    Thrown when a chaos scenario or plan fails to activate due to a runtime conflict or precondition violation that is not a configuration error.
    ChaosActivationHandle
    Live control handle for an activated chaos scenario.
    ChaosControlPlane
    Primary entry point to the chaos agent runtime.
    ChaosDecisionRecorder
    Records which matches of each scenario took effect, so a run can be replayed exactly with ActivationPolicy.Builder.replayMatches(java.util.Collection), even when it was driven by an unseeded probability.
    ChaosDiagnostics
    Read-only runtime view of all registered chaos scenarios and agent health.
    ChaosDiagnostics.ActivationFailure
    A record of a failed scenario activation attempt.
    ChaosDiagnostics.FailureCategory
    Categories of scenario activation failure, used for programmatic error handling.
    ChaosDiagnostics.ScenarioReport
    Per-scenario state and counters at snapshot time.
    ChaosDiagnostics.ScenarioState
    Lifecycle state of a registered chaos scenario.
    ChaosDiagnostics.Snapshot
    Immutable point-in-time snapshot of the full agent state.
    ChaosEffect
    Describes the chaos behavior applied when a scenario matches an invocation.
    ChaosEffect.AddressFamily
    The address family a ChaosEffect.DnsAnswerEffect keeps.
    ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect
    Skews the JVM clock as observed through System.currentTimeMillis() and System.nanoTime().
    ChaosEffect.ClockSkewMode
    Mode for ChaosEffect.ClockSkewEffect.
    ChaosEffect.CodeCachePressureEffect
    Fills the JVM code cache by generating and JIT-compiling a large number of unique synthetic classes.
    ChaosEffect.ConnectionResetEffect
    Closes the socket abortively (SO_LINGER 0): the peer sees a connection reset.
    ChaosEffect.CorruptReadEffect
    Flips exactly one bit in the bytes a successful read returned.
    ChaosEffect.DeadlockEffect
    Creates a deadlock between participantCount threads by acquiring locks in conflicting orders.
    ChaosEffect.DelayEffect
    Delays the matched operation by a random duration in [minDelay, maxDelay].
    ChaosEffect.DirectBufferPressureEffect
    Allocates off-heap direct ByteBuffers to exhaust native direct memory.
    ChaosEffect.DnsAnswerEffect
    Reshapes a DNS answer: replaces it (override, IP literals; applied even when the real lookup failed), keeps one address family, shuffles it and limits its size, in that order.
    ChaosEffect.DnsRewriteEffect
    Resolves host instead of the name the application asked for.
    ChaosEffect.Errno
    The errors an ChaosEffect.ErrnoEffect can raise, with the Java exception each becomes.
    ChaosEffect.Errno.Family
    Which operations an error belongs to.
    ChaosEffect.ErrnoEffect
    Fails the operation the way the operating system reports errno, as the Java exception an application catches for it — the native library's ERRNO effect.
    ChaosEffect.ExceptionalCompletionEffect
    Completes a matched CompletableFuture exceptionally before normal completion runs.
    ChaosEffect.ExceptionInjectionEffect
    Injects an exception at the entry of a matched method, before the method body executes.
    ChaosEffect.FailureKind
    Failure kind for ChaosEffect.ExceptionalCompletionEffect.
    ChaosEffect.FinalizerBacklogEffect
    Creates objects with slow finalizers to back up the finalizer queue.
    ChaosEffect.GateEffect
    Blocks the matched operation on a manual gate until the gate is opened or maxBlock elapses.
    ChaosEffect.GcPressureEffect
    Sustains a target allocation rate to create GC pressure.
    ChaosEffect.HeapPressureEffect
    Allocates and retains heap memory in chunks, simulating a memory leak or spike.
    ChaosEffect.KeepAliveEffect
    Keeps a named thread alive to simulate a thread that refuses to terminate.
    ChaosEffect.MetaspacePressureEffect
    Generates and loads synthetic classes to fill JVM Metaspace.
    ChaosEffect.MonitorContentionEffect
    Creates high contention on one shared ReentrantLock by spawning threads that repeatedly acquire and hold it, simulating lock convoy conditions.
    ChaosEffect.RedirectEffect
    Connects to another endpoint than the one the application asked for.
    ChaosEffect.ReferenceQueueFloodEffect
    Floods the ReferenceHandler thread's queue by creating a large number of WeakReference objects pointing to immediately-unreachable objects, then triggering GC.
    ChaosEffect.RejectEffect
    Rejects the matched operation the way the real call fails: by throwing the exception that call throws, inferred from the OperationType by the runtime (FailureFactory).
    ChaosEffect.ReturnValueCorruptionEffect
    Corrupts the return value of a matched method on exit.
    ChaosEffect.ReturnValueStrategy
    Strategy for ChaosEffect.ReturnValueCorruptionEffect.
    ChaosEffect.SafepointStormEffect
    Triggers repeated JVM safepoints by calling System.gc() at the configured rate, causing stop-the-world pauses.
    ChaosEffect.SpuriousWakeupEffect
    Causes Selector.select() to return 0 immediately with no ready keys, simulating a spurious wakeup.
    ChaosEffect.StringInternPressureEffect
    Interns a large number of unique strings, growing the JVM's string table: a long table slows every intern() of the application.
    ChaosEffect.SuppressEffect
    Skips the matched operation.
    ChaosEffect.ThreadLeakEffect
    Spawns threads that are intentionally never terminated.
    ChaosEffect.ThreadLocalLeakEffect
    Plants ThreadLocal entries in threads obtained from the common thread pool, simulating the most common form of ThreadLocal memory leak in production: pool threads retaining large request-scoped objects across requests.
    ChaosEffect.TimeoutEffect
    Waits for the socket's own timeout, then throws SocketTimeoutException; never fires when the timeout is infinite.
    ChaosEffect.TornWriteEffect
    Tears a write: a channel write succeeds short, a socket stream write is cut and reset.
    ChaosEffect.TrickleEffect
    Lets each socket read return at most maxBytes bytes.
    ChaosEffect.VirtualThreadCarrierPinningEffect
    Starts pinnedThreadCount virtual threads, each of which holds its carrier for pinDuration per cycle: on JDK 21–23 by sleeping inside a synchronized block (true pinning, no CPU), on JDK 24 and later, where synchronized no longer pins (JEP 491), by spin-waiting (one CPU per held carrier).
    ChaosEvent
    Immutable event published to ChaosEventListener subscribers on every chaos lifecycle transition and effect application.
    ChaosEvent.Type
    Discriminates the kind of chaos event delivered to ChaosEventListener.
    ChaosEventListener
    Observer for all chaos lifecycle and effect-application events.
    ChaosInstrumentationException
    Thrown when a scenario cannot be activated because the instrumentation it needs cannot be woven into the running JVM.
    ChaosMetricsSink
    Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
    a second metrics API beside the events: the same count is chaos.applications of chaos-agent-micrometer's ChaosMeterBinder and of chaos-agent-opentelemetry, which a ChaosEventListener on APPLIED events can also produce for any other backend.
    ChaosPlan
    An ordered, named collection of chaos scenarios that activate as a unit.
    ChaosPlan.Metadata
    Identity and human-readable description of a chaos plan.
    ChaosPlan.Observability
    Per-plan toggles for the built-in observability integrations.
    ChaosPresets
    Ready-made scenarios for the faults production systems actually meet: a full or failing disk, a refused or slow peer, packet loss, a DNS outage, a clock jump, exhausted descriptors or threads.
    ChaosScenario
    Immutable description of a single chaos injection scenario.
    ChaosScenario.Builder
    Fluent builder for ChaosScenario.
    ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope
    Defines the visibility scope of a scenario.
    ChaosSelector
    Defines the targeting predicate for a chaos scenario.
    ChaosSelector.AsyncSelector
    Matches CompletableFuture completion operations.
    ChaosSelector.AwsSdkSelector
    Matches AWS SDK for Java v2 operations, optionally by service and operation.
    ChaosSelector.ClassLoadingSelector
    Matches class and resource loading operations.
    ChaosSelector.DnsSelector
    Matches DNS resolution operations, optionally filtering by the hostname being resolved.
    ChaosSelector.ExecutorSelector
    Matches executor submit and worker-run operations, optionally filtering by executor class and submitted task class.
    ChaosSelector.FileIoSelector
    Matches file operations: reads and writes of streams, RandomAccessFile and FileChannel, fsync, truncation, deletion and moves.
    ChaosSelector.HttpClientSelector
    Matches HTTP client send operations across supported clients, optionally filtering by request URL.
    ChaosSelector.JdbcSelector
    Matches JDBC connection-pool and Connection / Statement operations, optionally filtering by a target-name pattern (pool identifier or SQL snippet).
    ChaosSelector.JvmRuntimeSelector
    Matches JVM runtime service calls: clock reads, GC requests, process exit, reflection invocations, direct buffer allocations, and object deserialization.
    ChaosSelector.MessagingSelector
    Matches messages sent and received through Kafka clients, optionally by topic.
    ChaosSelector.MethodSelector
    Matches entry to or exit from any method matching the class and method name patterns.
    ChaosSelector.MonitorSelector
    Matches monitor entry and thread parking operations, optionally filtering by the class of the object whose monitor is being entered.
    ChaosSelector.NettySelector
    Matches Netty channel reads and writes on any transport, optionally by the peer.
    ChaosSelector.NetworkSelector
    Matches socket/network operations, optionally filtering by remote host name or IP string.
    ChaosSelector.NioSelector
    Matches NIO channel and selector operations, optionally filtering by channel class name.
    ChaosSelector.ProcessSelector
    Matches the start of child processes and waits for them, optionally by program.
    ChaosSelector.QueueSelector
    Matches blocking queue operations, optionally filtering by queue implementation class.
    ChaosSelector.RedisSelector
    Matches Redis commands sent through Jedis or Lettuce, optionally by command name.
    ChaosSelector.RpcSelector
    Matches gRPC client calls, optionally by full method name (package.Service/Method).
    ChaosSelector.SchedulingSelector
    Matches scheduled task submission and tick operations.
    ChaosSelector.ShutdownSelector
    Matches JVM shutdown hook registration and executor shutdown operations.
    ChaosSelector.SslSelector
    Matches SSL/TLS handshake operations on both SSLSocket and SSLEngine.
    ChaosSelector.StressSelector
    Activates a standalone stressor effect.
    ChaosSelector.StressTarget
    Identifies which stressor to activate when using ChaosSelector.StressSelector.
    ChaosSelector.ThreadKind
    Classifies the thread type targeted by a ChaosSelector.ThreadSelector.
    ChaosSelector.ThreadLocalSelector
    Matches ThreadLocal get and set operations, optionally filtering by the ThreadLocal subclass name.
    ChaosSelector.ThreadSelector
    Matches thread start operations filtered by thread kind and name.
    ChaosSession
    A named session scope that restricts chaos effects to the threads bound to it.
    ChaosSession.ScopeBinding
    A handle that represents a thread's active binding to a ChaosSession.
    ChaosUnsupportedFeatureException
    Thrown when a chaos scenario requires a JVM feature or capability that is not available on the current runtime.
    ChaosValidationException
    Thrown during scenario activation when the scenario's configuration violates an API contract.
    CidrBlock
    A block of IP addresses in CIDR notation: "10.0.0.0/8", "2001:db8::/32", or a single address such as "192.168.1.10" (a /32 or /128 block).
    Internal
    Marks a type, method, field, or constructor as part of the chaos-agent's internal implementation.
    NamePattern
    A named string-matching predicate used by selectors to filter JVM operations by class name, method name, thread name, resource name, or any other string-valued attribute.
    NamePattern.MatchMode
    Determines the matching algorithm applied by NamePattern.matches(String).
    OperationType
    Identifies the JVM operation being intercepted or the lifecycle event being signalled.
    PathPattern
    Matches file paths under a directory, or one file.
